q: Lyapunov's second method for discrete-time systems: the system xₙ₊₁ = f(xₙ) is asymptotically stable at x* = 0 if there exists V with V(0) = 0, V(x) > 0 for x ≠ 0, and:
opts: V(f(x)) − V(x) < 0 for x ≠ 0 (ΔV < 0 — the discrete Lyapunov decrease condition)
exp: Discrete Lyapunov: ΔV(x) = V(f(x)) − V(x) < 0 for x ≠ 0 implies asymptotic stability. The discrete version is analogous to V̇ < 0 in continuous time, but care must be taken: ΔV < 0 is sufficient for A.S. but not strictly necessary in the same way as continuous time.
